data.title: Chinese Motor Tricycles Glide Into International Markets With Innovation, Customized Services
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 2 -- Sturdy, agile and capable of hauling almost anything -- this is the familiar image of Chinese motor tricycles that overseas consumers have come to recognize, riding the viral "Chinamaxxing" wave on social media.

Now, an expanding set of customizable options is further boosting the vehicle's international market appeal.

With customer-oriented services and innovative modifications, Chinese motor tricycle makers are moving beyond product exports to build deeper ties with overseas markets, creating new momentum for local industries while adapting to the needs of consumers abroad.

At a motor tricycle factory in Yanshi District of Luoyang, central China's Henan Province, a new vehicle rolls off the automated assembly line every 15 minutes. The tricycles can be customized to deliver parking warnings in both Chinese and English.

Zhang Jiwei, an employee at the factory, said the vehicles can be further tailored to meet different customers' needs.

"For Egyptian and UAE customers in the tourism industry, we offer passenger and sightseeing models with attractive designs and greater comfort. In Central Asia and Africa, tricycles are more commonly used to haul goods, so we often adjust cargo compartments and fuel-tank capacity of our products," Zhang said.

Such demand has helped drive the growth of Yanshi's motor tricycle industry. The district is home to 15 complete-vehicle manufacturers and more than 270 supporting parts companies, employing about 12,000 people and accounting for more than one-third of China's motor tricycle production capacity, according to local authorities.

Behind the customized service is a "half-hour parts supply circle," with most components -- except engines, tires, carburetors and lighting equipment -- sourced locally, said Ji Xianghui, head of the district's industry, information technology and commerce bureau.

In 2025, Yanshi produced and sold about 300,000 motor tricycles, including 98,000 exported vehicles, Ji said. In the first half of 2026, another 55,000 complete vehicles were exported, with the annual figure expected to reach 110,000, he added.

Customized products, however, are only part of the story behind the growing popularity of Chinese-made three-wheelers overseas.

In Fengxian County in east China's Jiangsu Province, another major production hub with about 1,400 related manufacturers, electric tricycles are winning over African consumers with a different combination of strengths: lower operating costs and greater versatility.

Meizida, an electric tricycle maker based in Fengxian, began selling its products in Cape Verde through distributors in 2020. Annual shipments have since grown from one or two containers to about five, with annual sales exceeding 200 vehicles, according to the company.

Compared with fuel-powered vehicles, the tricycles offer lower energy costs, more stable performance and easier maintenance, said Yu Baishun, the company's general manager. Compared with ordinary motorcycles, they also offer greater carrying capacity, he added.

The products have proved particularly suitable for small and micro businesses in Africa, where a single vehicle can be used to haul goods, commute or even serve as a mobile stall, Yu said.

In the first five months of 2026, electric tricycle exports from Fengxian reached 390 million yuan (about 57.9 million U.S. dollars), up 99.3 percent year on year, according to local statistics.

Together, the experiences of Yanshi and Fengxian show how different strengths of Chinese manufacturing are finding their way into overseas markets -- from flexible customization and efficient supply chains, to versatile electric models.

For these manufacturers, however, exporting vehicles is only the first step in their overseas expansion.

In Yanshi, manufacturers are partnering with overseas companies to establish warehouses and after-sales service outlets, developing a model that combines order-based exports with joint after-sales support.

Other tricycle producers are establishing production bases and direct-sales stores in several countries, building localized production and sales networks across Africa and South America.

Such moves reflect a broader shift in China's manufacturing exports. China's well-coordinated and large-scale supply chains allow companies to shorten the cycle from design and production to restocking and logistics, enabling faster and more flexible product development and iteration, said Li Kai, an associate professor at Xiamen University's School of Economics.

"For overseas consumers, that means access to more up-to-date, reliable products and services at competitive prices," he said.

The shift is in line with China's efforts to promote higher-quality foreign trade and support sustainable economic growth. The outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) calls for promoting trade innovation, improving the quality and efficiency of foreign trade, and expanding market diversification.

Yet the story of Chinese motor tricycles overseas goes beyond trade figures.

In the comment sections of buyer review videos on YouTube and other social media platforms, tricycle users from different parts of the world are sharing their experiences and memories of the vehicles.

"These small vehicles are everywhere where we live... When I was a little boy, my grandfather often rode one to take me to school," one viewer using a Chinese-language username commented.

"That's great for a large property and gardening, and for your kids learning how to drive too. Safer to learn on that than a tractor," another viewer replied.

"By choosing our products, customers are also finding connections with our everyday lives," Ji said.

In that sense, these humble three-wheelers offer a more down-to-earth glimpse of the country, beyond the image of the "world's factory" or technology giants' hub -- a place where innovation takes root in ordinary people's daily lives.

data.title: Global EV Giant BYD Deepens Shaanxi Push as Blade Battery Base Hits Full Production
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 30 -- BYD, the world's biggest electric vehicle maker, has begun full production at a new battery base in northwestern China's Shaanxi province, one of the first plants making its second-generation Blade Battery for ultra-fast charging.

The CNY7 billion (USD984 million) facility in Xixian New Area, a development zone between Xi’an and Xianyang, has an annual battery capacity of 16 gigawatt-hours, enough to supply about 700,000 new energy vehicles, according to local media reports. It is expected to generate CNY8 billion in annual output value.

BYD unveiled its second-generation Blade Battery and flash-charging technology in March, when the Xixian facility began trial production. The battery can charge from 10 percent to 70 percent in five minutes under normal temperatures, according to BYD.

The almost 89-hectare Xixian base was built at a rapid pace. Shaanxi is already home to BYD’s largest vehicle manufacturing hub by output capacity, with its Xi’an operations capable of producing more than one million vehicles a year.

Despite its relatively modest capacity, the Xixian base will help expand Shaanxi from a major BYD vehicle manufacturing center into a hub for next-generation batteries and flash-charging technology, Feng Lei, president of Huoshi Chuangzao Industrial Research Institute, told Yicai. Its 16 GWh of capacity will mainly serve BYD’s internal needs rather than external customers for now, he added.

BYD is also building a new energy vehicle parts project in Xixian New Area, according to local news outlet Xi’an Release. The roughly 81-hectare project will support BYD’s vehicle manufacturing operations and further increase the local supply of key components.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: Digital Twins Push Into Clinical Trials, but Data, Regulation Hold the Key
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept 28 -- Digital twins are finding their way into clinical trials as drugmakers explore their potential to predict treatment outcomes, though wider adoption will depend on sufficient patient data and regulatory acceptance.

In the past month, Chen Huan, founder of a medical modeling company, told Health Insight that the firm has received requests from four groups of clients, including pharmaceutical companies, contract research organizations, and hospitals, seeking artificial intelligence-powered virtual patients that can predict drug effects in early-stage clinical trials.

AI virtual patients have traditionally been used in medical education, but advances in large language models are expanding their use into clinical research. The technology can create a digital twin from a real patient's health data to simulate how their condition may evolve under different treatments, potentially improving clinical decisions and reducing research costs.

But wider use still faces hurdles. Limited patient data can make reliable models difficult to train, while generative AI's black-box nature makes its results difficult to interpret and trust.

Still, regulatory support is growing. In June, the US Food and Drug Administration issued guidelines allowing evidence from model-informed drug development to provide supplementary support for regulatory decisions. Five days later, China's National Medical Products Administration and three other government departments encouraged the use of virtual patients, or digital twins, to simulate and optimize treatment plans before real-world trials.

"This indicates a shift in regulatory consensus; digital twins are transitioning from being a single-point modeling tool to an early clinical decision support system," Chen said, adding that the shift is behind the recent surge in client demand. Virtual patients have had clear potential buyers from the outset, he added, as the technology ultimately targets pharmaceutical companies' clinical development budgets.

The technology is already drawing interest from hospitals. Qilu Hospital of Shandong University recently announced plans to procure a "digital twin virtual clinical trial" system for virtual population modeling and efficacy prediction. The project has a budget of CNY2.6 million (USD387,300).

China alone had nearly 3,000 new drug clinical trials in 2025. If just 20 percent of trial projects eventually use the technology and each project generates CNY2 million in service fees, the potential market would exceed CNY1 billion (USD149 million).

From Control Groups to Digital Twins

The approach differs fundamentally from conventional clinical trials.

Traditional clinical trials compare similar patient groups receiving different treatments, while digital twins seek to predict how a virtual version of the same patient would respond, according to Xu Liang, a senior AI pharmaceutical industry professional.

Patient information is often fragmented and stored in different formats, including medical records, pathology reports, imaging, genetic data, time series, and doctors' notes, making it difficult to analyze collectively. Xu said that LLMs are beginning to map this diverse information into a unified physiological trajectory for individual patients.

"At this point, the technology side has at least been able to make this work," the medical expert noted.

Data Hurdles Remain

Technical feasibility, however, does not mean the technology is suitable for every disease.

Digital twin technology must first identify suitable clinical trial scenarios if it is to advance further, according to Chen from the medical modeling company. Early research has focused on neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and Huntington's disease because they have clear longitudinal scales, continuous disease progression, and extensive historical clinical trial data.

By contrast, conditions are not yet mature for applying digital twins to rare diseases and cancers, despite strong demand for the technology, Chen said. Rare diseases in particular could benefit from reducing reliance on control groups but face a data paradox.

"Because there are few patients, we need digital twins; however, conversely, the scarcity of patients means there is limited data available, making it difficult to train reliable models," Chen said.

Generative AI also operates as a black box, making its results difficult to interpret and trust.

"Data determines whether a model can be developed, while regulation determines how much that model will ultimately be valued," Xu said, pointing to the two factors that will shape their wider use.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: China’s Geely, Nio Strengthen Battery-Swap Alliance With Cross-Shareholding Deal
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 28 -- Chinese automotive giant Geely Holding Group and electric vehicle manufacturer Nio will deepen their strategic cooperation on battery swapping and EV charging through a cross-shareholding arrangement at the subsidiary level, aimed at accelerating the expansion of their battery-swap and charging service networks.

Geely will use its 100 percent equity in its battery-swap service provider Yiyi Internet Technology and CNY640 million (USD95.3 million) in cash to subscribe to newly issued shares in Nio’s battery-swap and charging unit Nio Power, Shanghai-based Nio said today. Upon completion of the transaction, Geely will hold a 30 percent stake in Nio Power, which will have a post-investment valuation of CNY16 billion (USD2.4 billion).

Nio was one of the earliest Chinese EV manufacturers to adopt battery swapping and set up Nio Power in 2017 to develop and run a battery-swap and charging service network. As of Sept. 20, Nio operated 4,099 battery-swap stations and 5,289 charging stations, and had provided users with over 120 million battery swaps in total, it said.

Yiyi, founded in 2017, managed more than 470 battery-swap stations in over 40 cities across China as of April last year, and has plans to expand to 2,000 stations by next year, according to its website.

The integration of Yiyi into Nio Power will accelerate the expansion of Nio's battery swapping network, with the aim of building 10,000 battery-swap stations by 2030, Nio said. The two sides will also work together to establish unified battery-swapping technology standards, while Hangzhou-based Geely will develop battery-swap vehicles models for consumers.

Nio will also acquire a stake in Geely’s EV charging service provider Zhejiang Haohan Energy Technology, according to the agreement between the two parties. Upon completion of the transaction, Nio will hold a 10 percent stake in Haohan, and both sides will share resources to expand charging network coverage and improve operational efficiency.

Haohan currently operates 2,500 charging stations and 12,000 charging guns in 232 cities across China. By the end of 2027, it plans to expand its network to 22,000 charging stations and 100,000 charging guns, Geely said.

The collaboration between Nio and Geely dates back to November 2023, when Nio announced plans to form a battery swapping alliance with automakers. Since then, it has established partnerships with eight automakers, including Changan Automobile and Geely.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: China Fortune Land Development Shares Pare Gains on AI Firm Restructuring Deal
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 30 -- Shares of debt-laden China Fortune Land Development gave back some of their gains following a two-day rally after the Chinese property developer unveiled details of a restructuring deal that will bring in a new controlling shareholder linked to an artificial intelligence computing-power company.

CFLD [SHA: 600340] closed 5.1 percent lower at CNY1.30 (US 20 cents) today after rising over 6 percent yesterday and more than 10 percent the previous day. The shares remain 11 percent higher than before the planned controlling shareholder change was announced.

The property developer announced on Sept. 28 that Chengfeng Erjin Enterprise Management Partnership, an investment entity of cloud solution provider Chengfeng Erlai Digital Technology, and property firm Mulan Garden Real Estate signed a restructuring agreement with CFLD.

Founded in 2023 with registered capital of CNY500 million (USD74.6 million), Chengfeng Erlai mainly provides solutions related to large-model applications and AI computing power.

Under the agreement, Chengfeng Erjin will spend CNY1.2 billion (USD178.9 million) to acquire nearly two billion shares, while Mulan Real Estate will pay CNY600,000 (USD89,500) for one million shares. Together, the investors will hold almost 20.6 percent of CFLD after the transfers.

Chengfeng Erjin will be entitled to nominate or recommend at least six candidates for non-independent and independent director positions, with one of its nominees to serve as chairman after the restructuring. Chengfeng Erjin will become CFLD’s controlling shareholder through the restructuring investment, according to the announcement.

Heavy Debt Burden

CFLD has been struggling under a heavy debt burden. A creditor applied to a court in November last year to restructure the property developer and begin pre-restructuring proceedings, citing the company’s failure to repay debts when due and apparent inability to meet its obligations. As of Aug. 31, CFLD had about CNY28.4 billion (USD4.2 billion) in overdue debt, excluding interest.

The new partners could complement each other in some areas. Computing-power companies and property developers can create synergies in some industrial park projects, Liu Shui, director of enterprise research at the China Index Academy, told Yicai. Developers’ property resources and project development, construction, and operating capabilities can support data and intelligent computing centers, though not all existing land is suitable for such uses, Liu added.

However, the restructuring deal is not yet guaranteed to proceed. The agreement still faces risks of termination, rescission, revocation, or inability to be performed, the announcement added.

CFLD continues to face significant financial pressure. Operating revenue fell 43 percent from a year earlier to CNY1.7 billion in the first half of this year, while net loss attributable to shareholders of the company was CNY4.7 billion. As of the end of June, net assets attributable to shareholders stood at negative CNY21.8 billion.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: China Clears Four More AI Agent Smartphones for Network Access
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 30 -- Four more artificial intelligence agent smartphones received network access approval from the Chinese government yesterday, following the Nubia NaviX Ultra, equipped with the Doubao Mobile Assistant, which became the first AI agent mobile phone to obtain telecom equipment access approval late last month.

Three of the four AI agent smartphones are models from Honor’s Magic 9 series, while the fourth is the STEPX Neo, the first AI agent mobile phone built natively around a large language model and developed by STEPX, which is a subsidiary of LLM developer StepFun, according to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology’s website.

The approval and launch of multiple AI agent smartphones mark the point at which handsets that had previously been showcased mainly at product launch events and technological demonstrations are now entering the market for testing.

Unlike conventional mobile phones that have added AI features such as question answering and image generation, AI agent mobile phones seek to fundamentally change how users interact with their devices. After a user assigns a task, the agent can interpret the request, access system functions and third-party applications as well as carry out a series of actions autonomously.

Yicai noted significant differences in how the three companies are implementing AI agents. Honor has added a system-level Agent Harness framework to its self-developed MagicOS operating system to support agent orchestration. STEPX has developed a LLM-native AI agent smartphone. Meanwhile, Doubao uses a phone-assistant model to enable AI to directly operate third-party applications at the application level.

As smartphone replacement cycles lengthen and the overall market remains under pressure, handset makers are in need of new product selling points. However, whether AI can become a compelling enough reason for consumers to upgrade their devices remains to be tested by the market.

China’s smartphone shipments slumped 4.2 percent in the first half from a year ago to approximately 134 million units, according to US market research firm IDC.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Kim Taylor

data.title: AI Outpaces Training, Leaving Workers Facing a ‘Triple Capability Gap,’ Pearson Says
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 30 -- Artificial intelligence is reshaping skilled trade, technical and service jobs faster than education and training systems can adapt, opening up a "triple capability gap" that puts a new generation of workers at risk of becoming "AI-rich but experience-poor," according to a study recently released by UK education group Pearson, whose business spans digital and traditional contents assessment and certification.

The three capabilities, are "role-specific AI literacy and critical judgement, in other words being able to understand when to use AI, when to question it and how to apply it safely and responsibly, the human capabilities of communication, collaboration, adaptability, emotional intelligence and learning agility, and the institutional knowledge that retiring experts are taking with them," according to Pearson’s research, which was released on Sept. 24 during the 48th WorldSkills Competition in Shanghai that ended yesterday.

If left unaddressed, the gap "could make it harder for employers to maintain safety standards, sustain essential services and support economic growth," London-based Pearson said in two reports, namely the global report "For Every Future: Preparing Early-Career Skilled Trade, Technical and Service Talent for an AI-Infused World" and the "China Spotlight Report." 

A survey of trainee industrial machinery mechanics and other early-career workers found that most expect to use AI on the job, but “fewer than half indicated that they were even moderately confident that their training will prepare them to do so.”

Pearson, whose business spans assessment and certification, including BTEC vocational qualifications and Certiport technology certifications, was a platinum partner at this year’s WorldSkills Competition. Held for the first time in China, the event brought together 1,385 competitors from 68 countries and regions to compete in 64 events.

Skills Shortage

"Demand is rising as expertise walks out the door," Pearson said on a webpage dedicated to the global report, which compares labor markets in the US, UK and China. 

In the US, "these roles generate around 14.3 million job openings every year, and about 14.1 million of them, or 98.5 percent, come from replacing workers who retire, change occupation or leave the labor force altogether. In the UK, replacement demand is expected to total just over 4 million over the decade, equivalent to 99 percent of all openings," the global report said.

For China, our projections for skilled trade, technical and service workers indicate that demand will rise from around 347 million workers in 2023 to about 477 million by 2035, while the working-age population peaks and thus the supply of such workers falls to around 328 million. The result is a structural shortfall of roughly 149 million, it added.

"Even with the most optimistic combination of workforce measures, ranging from higher participation rates in the labor market to a greater number of graduates taking up skilled trades, technical and service jobs, the gap cannot be closed completely. The remainder must come from making each worker more productive, and AI has a significant role to play toward boosting worker productivity," the global report said. The China Spotlight Report specifically noted that the shortfall does not equal the number of job vacancies, but rather shows that supply-side measures alone cannot meet demand.

By sector, the occupations most driving this upward trend are within wholesale and retail, which is projected to increase by 92 percent, and culture, sports and entertainment, where hiring requirements are expected to double, the global report said.

Workforce Shift

The China Spotlight Report's industry analysis also showed that manufacturing, transportation, hotels and catering, and construction are more oriented toward automation, while wholesale and retail, health and social services, household services as well as culture, sports and entertainment show greater potential for AI augmentation.

"We are entering a period where workers across hospitals, factories and critical infrastructure will need to combine the judgement needed to work effectively with AI, the human skills that technology cannot replace, and the hands-on expertise gained through experience," Elaine Cao, chief executive officer of Pearson China.

"China has made a strong start, with industry-education integration, experience-first learning and purpose-built AI systems providing a strong foundation for an AI-enabled skilled workforce. Closing China's workforce readiness gap will require employers, educators and policymakers to move in step to help early-career workers grow alongside AI," she said.

"It was very, very common sentiment that the white collar jobs were the first place to look for where AI was going to have an impact," Art Valentine, president of Pearson’s Assessment and Qualifications business, told media outlets including Yicai. “But AI is already being used in frontline settings in manufacturing, healthcare and pharmacies for quality checks, process guidance and prescription verification. It is everywhere and it is not going to stop," he said.

Training Gap

On why vocational colleges are struggling to keep pace with market demand, Valentine said this is a common issue globally because "employers often have the ability to invest faster in what's happening in their market than the education system can." Schools should make sure that the students are getting their hands on those tools in the classroom in a way that is not theoretical but is specific to their field, and maintain ongoing dialogue with local employers, he added.

The same day, Valentine held a discussion with David Hoey, CEO of WorldSkills International, at a forum hosted by Pearson. Valentine outlined two approaches to assessment in the AI era, which are having candidates interact with AI tools in simulated or real-world work scenarios to gauge their judgment, or isolating candidates from AI and using written exams or oral questioning.

Hoey said the assessment of skills competitions has evolved from being almost entirely focused on technical abilities to increasingly incorporating soft skills such as decision-making and communication. Speaking about AI, he said: “It's not gonna go away. We gotta learn how to harness it. We've got to learn how to use it.”

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: China’s AI Users Top 700 Million as Adoption Rate Exceeds 50%, Report Shows
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 30 -- The ranks of generative artificial intelligence users in China surpassed 700 million in the first half, with AI adoption exceeding 50 percent, while all of the top six models on a mainstream global AI usage ranking were Chinese, according to a a new report.

Chatbot remained the most common use of genAI, the report published yesterday by the China Internet Network Information Center showed. Seventy-six percent of users said they use genAI for answers, while 48 percent use it to process images or videos, 38 percent for text processing, and 36 percent for work summaries, meeting minutes, or presentations. Usage of AI assistants and AI productivity tools more than doubled from a year earlier.

Smart hardware has also become an important channel for AI applications to reach consumers. In the past six months, 39 percent of Chinese internet users bought smart hardware online, including 20 percent who purchased wearable devices and 18 percent who bought 3C (computers, communications, and consumer) digital products such as smartphones and tablets.

Chinese companies including DeepSeek and Moonshot AI have released a number of open-source AI systems with trillions of parameters, while Chinese models are accelerating their adaptation to domestically developed AI chips, the report said.

The top six models on a mainstream global AI model usage ranking were developed by Chinese teams, it also pointed out. Public data from OpenRouter shows that Chinese AI systems, including Xiaomi’s MiMo-V2.5, DeepSeek V4 Flash, Tencent’s HY3, DeepSeek V4 Pro, and Z.AI’s GLM-5.2, ranked among the top in July.

AI applications now encompass industries such as steel, nonferrous metals, power, and telecoms, and have expanded into areas including product development, quality inspection, and customer service, according to the report.

More than 30 percent of Chinese manufacturers above a designated size had adopted AI technologies as of June, the report said. AI is being increasingly used across manufacturing processes, including research and development, production, quality inspection, and maintenance. China had more than 400 humanoid robot products in the first half, with full-year output expected to exceed 100,000 units, the report said.

China had 1,255 AI-related investment and financing deals in the six months ended June 30, equivalent to about 78 percent of the total for the whole of last year. The combined value reached about CNY250 billion (USD37.3 billion), or 182 percent of 2025’s figure, according to the report.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: China’s Appliance Makers Scale Back Discounting Ahead of ‘Golden Week’ Holiday Sales
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 30 -- China's National Day holiday, a “Golden Week” that begins tomorrow, is a key sales period for appliances, though manufacturers and retailers are showing little enthusiasm for aggressive discounting this time as rising costs, weak consumer confidence, and a soft housing market limit the effectiveness of price-led promotions.

The nation’s home appliance makers and retailers are instead prioritizing premium products, product upgrades, quality improvements, and customer experience, according to industry sources.

“With the long holiday coinciding with government subsidies for home appliance trade-ins, the National Day break remains a rare and valuable promotional window for the year," said Ge Sen, secretary-general of the Shanghai Household Electric Appliance Professional Association. He predicts a rebound in footfall at appliance experience stores in major shopping districts over the seven-day holiday.

Still, higher store traffic may not translate into stronger sales. Demand for major household appliances will remain weak because consumer confidence has yet to fully recover, according to Wang Hongji, head of home appliance research and insights at NIQ GfK China, a market intelligence services provider. For Golden Week retail sales, he forecasts year-on-year declines of 5.9 percent for televisions, 3.9 percent for washing machines, and 9 percent for air conditioners.

Manufacturers are also approaching holiday promotions cautiously. Some mid-range and premium models may see some moderate discounting, but mass-market products are unlikely to be marked down aggressively just to generate higher sales, an AC retailer in South China said.

“Relying solely on low prices to drive volume holds little value for either manufacturers or retailers at the moment,” the person noted. While consumers have become more cautious this year, they still prioritize quality, so businesses are more likely to use targeted discounts on premium offerings to stimulate broader demand, the retailer said.

In addition, sustained increases in raw material costs are straining profitability at manufacturers, leaving them with limited room to lower prices on mass-market products, the person added.

A regional sales manager at a TV maker in South China said rising production costs have prompted companies to focus their Golden Week sales strategies on promoting newly launched and upgraded products rather than competing on price.

The home appliance trade-in subsidy policy has been implemented for three years, causing some consumer demand to be pulled forward, he pointed out. Combined with ongoing weakness in China's property sector, the industry is unlikely to see a major surge in demand over the holiday, he said, adding that the modest decline in the market is expected to continue, reinforcing the company's emphasis on newly introduced products.

"Simply lowering prices is no longer enough to drive market or brand growth," said Liu Wenjuan, general manager of Yongsheng Home Appliances. She explained that a new generation of young consumers prioritizes the sense of quality and emotional value a product offers, making price a secondary concern.

The manager of a home appliance store in Nanfeng county, Jiangxi province told Yicai that since young people returning home for the holiday typically buy mid-to-high-end products, its flagship outlet is focusing holiday sales efforts on high-end models that offer healthy profit margins.

"The home appliance industry is shifting from pure price-based competition to competition based on experience and value -- a positive development for both consumers and the industry," said a representative for Midea's China business.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: Far Greater Priority Should be Given to AI Security, Insider Says
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 29 -- The capabilities of artificial intelligence models are growing at a frightening pace but global investment in developing the security systems needed to keep AI under control is far from adequate, an industry expert has warned.

“Rather than expanding the boundaries of model capabilities, we should focus more energy and resources on testing the reliability and security of models. This is what we should start doing today,” Zhang Hongjiang, an investment partner at Chinese venture capital firm Source Code Capital and an expert in the computer field, said in an interview with Yicai during the recent FutureChina Global Forum in Singapore.

Zhang has a strong industry background, having served as chief technology officer for Microsoft Asia-Pacific Research and Development Group and chief executive officer of Kingsoft Corporation. He also founded the Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence in 2018 and still serves as its founding chairman.

AI Security Risks Are Growing

In July, a cutting-edge agent model from US firm OpenAI "escaped" during testing. It bypassed the isolated sandbox constraints and hacked the open-source platform Hugging Face, signaling that AI may have crossed some red lines, Zhang said.

“For me, this is a very important event, not because of how much harm it has caused, but because this model was designed without malicious intent,” Zhang stated, adding this is even more concerning because “it has the ability to design its own behaviors without realizing the risks involved.”

AI models are now capable of achieving gold-medal results in the International Mathematical Olympiad, meaning that a general-purpose model without specialized training can outperform most professionals on specialized problems, Zhang pointed out.

"When an AI’s IQ exceeds 140 and it is backed by a powerful knowledge base, its capabilities become immense, and that is a frightening prospect," he noted.

Safety More Important Than Competition

AI is entering a highly competitive stage, and countries and companies are competing to launch ever more advanced models. In this context, we cannot rely on individual countries or institutions to “self-restrain,” Zhang said, and we must establish cross-border coordination and supervision mechanisms that prioritize security.

Zhang mentioned nuclear safety as an example. In order to prevent disasters like the Chernobyl nuclear power plant accident from happening again, the majority of research funding for nuclear power plants is now dedicated to safety. But controlling AI is more difficult than nuclear power regulation, he warned.

Nuclear tests and facilities leave physical traces that can be verified through multiple sources such as satellite imagery and seismic monitoring, but the form of AI models is software, which makes tracking more difficult.

Also, nuclear testing is mostly in the hands of a limited number of national institutions, while AI models are being developed by companies all over the world whose priority is commercial success and strong market positions, making security more complicated, Zhang explained.

While it is true that if one nation pauses its progress, another may catch up, a "zero-sum" mindset is inappropriate for AI, given how profound and wide-ranging its influence will be in society. "National interests must yield in the face of risks to humanity's future survival," Zhang said.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Tom Litting

data.title: Xpeng-Backed Flying Car Giant Aridge Partners With UAE to Set Up Regulatory Sandbox
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 22 -- Aridge, the flying car company backed by Chinese new energy vehicle giant Xpeng Group, formerly known as Xpeng AeroHT, has reached a deal with officials of the United Arab Emirates to establish a regulatory cooperation mechanism for air traffic.

Aridge and the Emirate of Ras Al Khaimah agreed to jointly set up an air traffic regulatory sandbox platform under the UAE General Civil Aviation Authority to promote the airworthiness certification and commercialization of low-altitude flying products in the Middle East, the Guangzhou-based company announced on Sept. 20.

Aridge will leverage the regulatory sandbox mechanism to conduct systematic flight testing in typical scenarios in the Middle East, focusing on collecting data about the aircraft performance, including power performance, endurance, airspace adaptability, and operational safety risks, under special environmental conditions, such as high temperatures and sandstorms. The company aims to complete localized adaptation verification.

Moreover, Aridge will carry out specialized feasibility verification for commercial deployment in diverse application scenarios, including high-end tourism and sightseeing, urban short-distance air transit, emergency rescue operations, and offshore oil platform inspections.

Aridge was founded in 2013 as Huitian. Xpeng and its founder He Xiaopeng invested in the company in 2020. Aridge has developed the Land Aircraft Carrier, the world's first modular flying car that combines electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft with automobiles. It achieved mass production and roll-out in March and is expected to launch within the year.

There is no unified flying car sandbox system in the Chinese mainland, an analyst told Yicai. However, six cities -- Hefei, Hangzhou, Shenzhen, Suzhou, Chengdu, and Chongqing -- have approved eVTOL pilot programs, opening up market opportunities for commercial passenger flights, the person added.

By 2040, the Chinese and overseas eVTOL markets are expected to reach USD41 billion and USD184 billion, respectively, presenting significant market opportunities for manufacturers, according to a report released by Boston Consulting Group last year. As a global hub for luxury consumption, the Middle East is emerging as a potential market for passenger eVTOLs.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Futura Costaglione

data.title: Chinese Fashion E-Retailer SHEIN Sinks as First-Half Profit Plunges Over 50% Despite More Orders
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 29 -- Shares in SHEIN Global Holdings plunged today after the Chinese online fast-fashion and lifestyle retailer reported a more than 50 percent drop in profit in the first six months from a year earlier, despite an increase in total orders, as higher oil prices and freight costs weighed on earnings.

SHEIN’s share price [HKG: 0625] sank 10.4 percent to end the day at HKD31.58 (USD4).

The firm’s operating profit plummeted 52.9 percent in the six months ended June 30 from a year ago to USD493 million, while adjusted net profit dived 55.6 percent to USD499 million, according to the interim report released by the Singapore-based firm yesterday. Net revenue climbed 1 percent to USD20.1 billion.

Profitability was affected by higher oil prices and freight costs, which SHEIN absorbed to maintain a consistent pricing experience and order momentum, it said.

In the second quarter, adjusted net profit plunged 66.6 percent year on year to USD228 million, while net revenue edged up 0.9 percent to USD11.1 billion.

Second-quarter revenue growth was partly moderated by a higher marketplace mix, under which it recognizes service revenue rather than the full value of products sold, the firm said.

Despite the drop in profitability, SHEIN's total orders gained 6.4 percent in the first six months from the same period last year to 549 million, including a 7.6 percent increase to 298 million in the second quarter. Active customers soared 14.5 percent in the 12 months ended June 30 from a year earlier to 291 million.

Looking ahead, SHEIN's management team has identified three priorities for the next one to two years, namely expanding its price range, increasing investment in quality and compliance, and strengthening communication with consumers.

SHEIN sees an opportunity to broaden consumer choice by expanding its product mix to include brands at higher price points, it said. As the product mix shifts toward higher-priced brands, the platform's average selling price is expected to rise and improve profitability, while the firm will continue to maintain and optimize products across existing price ranges.

SHEIN expects its overall average selling price to rise as its product mix expands toward brands at higher price points, founder and Chairman Sky Xu said. The company will continue to maintain its value-for-money positioning across existing price ranges, he added.

SHEIN said it plans to increase investment in product quality, compliance and corporate transparency. These efforts will strengthen consumer confidence and provide greater clarity on the efficiency gains underpinning its business model, it added. The firm will also step up communication with consumers through improvements to its app and a more deliberate approach to brand marketing.

By region, SHEIN's second-quarter revenue in the US slumped 4 percent year on year to USD2.5 billion. The company said its US business was continuing to recover from the impact of tariffs.

Revenue in Europe tumbled 16.1 percent in the three months ended June 30 from the year before to USD3.7 billion. The firm has raised prices and cut online advertising spending in the region ahead of the European Union's planned removal of the EUR150 (USD170) low-value goods duty exemption, it said.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: China's Hengrui Gains After Licensing Weight-Loss Drug to Novo Nordisk in up to USD2.6 Billion Deal
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 29 -- Shares of Hengrui Pharmaceuticals rose today after the Chinese drugmaker licensed the overseas rights to an investigational oral weight-loss drug to Danish pharmaceutical giant Novo Nordisk in a deal worth up to USD2.6 billion.

Hengrui [SHA: 600276] closed 2.6 percent higher at CNY45.62 (USD6.80) in Shanghai after rising as much as 3.7 percent intraday. Its Hong Kong-listed shares [HK: 01276] advanced 1.9 percent to HKD45.60 (USD5.80).

Hengrui has granted Novo Nordisk exclusive rights to develop, manufacture, and commercialize HRS-1596, its investigational once-weekly oral glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) dual receptor agonist, outside the Chinese mainland, Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan, the Jiangsu province-headquartered company announced today.

HRS-1596 is a GLP-1/GIP dual receptor agonist independently developed by Hengrui that aims to reduce weight and improve blood glucose control through multiple mechanisms, including suppressing appetite, promoting insulin secretion, and improving insulin sensitivity, according to the announcement.

The agreement with Novo Nordisk will help provide high-quality treatment options to patients worldwide and enable HRS-1596 to rapidly expand into overseas markets with the support of a leading international partner, Hengrui said.

The licensing collaboration will also help Hengrui accelerate its integration into the global pharmaceutical innovation network and maximize the value of its products, the company added.

The potential value of the deal is up to USD2.6 billion, including an upfront payment of USD300 million and milestone payments tied to the achievement of key development, regulatory, and commercialization targets. Hengrui will also be eligible for royalties based on a percentage of net sales of HRS-1596 in the licensed territories.

The drug candidate has the potential to treat obesity, type 2 diabetes, and other metabolic diseases, Hengrui said. Compared with existing treatment options, HRS-1596 could significantly reduce dosing frequency and improve treatment convenience, it added. HRS-1596 has been approved in China to begin Phase I clinical trials for weight management and the treatment of type 2 diabetes.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: China to Develop Commercial Satellites Specifically for Space Breeding
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 24 -- China is moving to establish a dedicated commercial satellite platform for seed breeding in space, rather than continuing to rely mainly on spare capacity aboard other satellites and space missions.

The initiative, launched by the Shaanxi Aerospace Breeding Engineering Technology Research Center and Zhongke Satellite Technology Group, is intended to make space mutagenesis experiments more customizable, scalable, and accessible to researchers and breeders. Shaanxi provincial authorities made the announcement yesterday.

“There’s been no dedicated satellite platform specifically designed for biological space mutagenesis, making it difficult to customize or scale up experimental payloads, in-orbit durations, and testing conditions,” said Guo Rui, the research center’s director. “China's aerospace breeding experiments have relied on piggybacking on existing satellites or utilizing space station missions.”

The development and launch of a dedicated commercial space-breeding satellite will give seeds traveling into space their own “exclusive transport,” he noted.

Space breeding, also known as space mutagenesis, is an agricultural technique where plant seeds or other plant materials are sent into orbit to be exposed to environmental conditions that cannot be fully reproduced on Earth. Once back on the ground, they are screened to identify useful heritable mutations and develop new crop varieties.


Shaanxi Aerospace Breeding and Zhongke Satellite have also signed an agreement to jointly establish a Joint Laboratory for Space Biological Mutagenesis, the announcement said. Set up in Xi'an University, the lab is a collaborative effort involving universities, research institutions, and commercial aerospace businesses, creating an open and shared innovation platform.

“Deep participation by commercial aerospace companies in space breeding is an important example of how space technology can drive 'new quality productive forces' in the agricultural sector,” said Zhang Zhihao, director of the Qiming Laboratory at Zhongke Satellite.

“New quality productive forces” is a Chinese policy term that refers broadly to new forms of economic productivity driven by technological innovation, advanced industries, and higher-quality growth, rather than simply increasing inputs such as labor, land, or capital.

Jinan-based Zhongke Satellite will draw on its capabilities in satellite development, launch, tracking and control, and in-orbit operations to support development of the dedicated breeding-satellite platform and provide research teams with stable and reliable conditions for space-based experiments, Zhang said.


Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: CXMT to Invest USD5.2 Billion to Enhance R&D, Memory Wafer Testing Capabilities
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 29 -- Shares of Changxin Memory Technologies rose after the Chinese DRAM chipmaker said it will invest CNY35 billion (USD5.2 billion) to enhance its memory wafer testing and new product research and development capabilities, with much of the financing sourced from excess proceeds of its July initial public offering.

CXMT [SHA: 688825] finished up 3.3 percent at CNY55.55 (USD8.28) per share in Shanghai today.

Of the total investment, CNY24.1 billion will go to setting up a 12-inch memory wafer R&D base in Hefei, with construction taking 30 months, the Hefei-based company said late yesterday. CNY10.8 billion will be used for a new wafer testing plant at another site in the city that will provide testing and module assembly services for dynamic random-access memory chips. Its construction will take 37 months.

The filing did not disclose further details of the two projects, such as key R&D focuses of the first project and the annual capacity for the wafer testing and module assembly project. It only stated that the R&D base project will receive CNY 13 billion in support from excess IPO proceeds, while the wafer testing plant project will get CNY 5 billion of such funds.

The AI-fueled boom and resulting shortage of memory chips have buoyed investor optimism over Changxin Memory Technologies’ business outlook. The firm completed its IPO on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in late July, raising far more than its target fundraising amount. After exercising the green shoe option and deducting various issuance costs, its net proceeds stood at CNY 66.3 billion, with excess IPO proceeds totaling CNY 36.8 billion. The ample capital provides support for the company to invest in more projects.

The new R&D project will help CXMT maintain its technological edge and accelerate the introduction of products that more closely match demand, deliver better performance, and offer greater competitiveness, it said. The company expects the project, in turn, to strengthen its core competitiveness and resilience to business risks.

The new testing facility will help address two potential constraints: insufficient testing capacity at external chip packaging-and-testing providers, and a potential shortage of in-house testing capacity as CXMT expands wafer production, the company said. Bringing more testing capacity in-house will also reduce the cost of checking the firm’s DRAM chips, it added.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: China's Akeso Soars as AstraZeneca Backs Cancer Drug Partner Summit With USD2 Billion
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 29 -- Shares of Akeso surged after global pharmaceutical giant AstraZeneca agreed to provide USD2 billion in finance American oncology company Summit Therapeutics, which holds the overseas rights to the Chinese drugmaker’s cancer therapy ivonescimab.

Akeso [HK: 9926] closed up 15.5 percent at HKD106.30 (USD13.55) in Hong Kong after surging by more than 17 percent intraday.

Zhongshan-based Akeso developed ivonescimab and licensed its development and commercialization rights in major overseas markets to Summit in 2022.

AstraZeneca will invest USD2 billion in newly issued convertible preferred shares in Summit to accelerate ivonescimab’s development, Akeso said today, citing announcements by AstraZeneca and Summit. The two companies will also collaborate on trials combining ivonescimab with AstraZeneca’s antibody drug conjugates (ADCs) across tumour types.

Ivonescimab is a potential first-in-class bispecific antibody that simultaneously blocks PD-1, helping the immune system attack cancer cells, and VEGF, which tumors use to grow new blood vessels. The drug is approved in China for certain patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), while Summit is developing it in overseas markets including the United States, Europe and Japan.

Akeso licensed Summit ivonescimab’s development and commercialization rights in major overseas markets in December 2022 in exchange for upfront and milestone payments of up to USD5 billion, plus double-digit royalties on net sales after the drug reaches the market. At the time, it was the largest overseas licensing deal for a single innovative drug from China.

AstraZeneca Takes Stake

The latest investment values Summit shares at USD18.36 each upon conversion, 10 percent above the prior week’s five-day volume-weighted average price and a premium to its Sept. 28 close, giving AstraZeneca about 12 percent of Summit.

Michelle Xia, founder and chairwoman of Akeso, said AstraZeneca’s strategic investment in Summit is expected to provide funding and industry resources to accelerate the global clinical development of ivonescimab, including in China.

According to Summit President and Co-Chief Executive Maky Zanganeh, the AstraZeneca deal will broaden ivonescimab’s development and support new trials combining its PD-1/VEGF approach, which helps the immune system attack tumors while cutting off their blood supply, with other promising cancer treatments, including antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), which deliver drugs directly to cancer cells.

Expanding Ivonescimab Trials

Under the clinical collaboration, Summit and AstraZeneca will test ivonescimab together with sonesitatug vedotin, an ADC designed to deliver cancer-killing drugs to cells carrying the Claudin-18.2 protein. Trials of the combination in certain gastrointestinal cancers are expected to begin soon, with AstraZeneca sponsoring the studies and both companies sharing the costs.

The two companies also signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding to potentially establish a broader global clinical program combining ivonescimab with other AstraZeneca cancer medicines, including additional ADCs. Each company will retain its existing development and commercial rights to its respective medicines.

In the US, the Food and Drug Administration is reviewing an application to approve ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy for NSCLC patients with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations. The drug is also in Phase III trials for several cancers, including small-cell lung, biliary tract, bladder, triple-negative breast, head and neck, colorectal, and pancreatic cancers.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: Chinese Firms Dominate Global Humanoid Robot Revenue Ranking, Frost & Sullivan Says
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 29 -- Chinese companies took all five top spots in the global ranking by humanoid robot revenue from 2025 through the first half of this year, according to Frost & Sullivan.

The five companies together accounted for more than 50 percent of the global market, the consultancy said in its 2026 humanoid robot market report. Global sales reached 36,000 units in the first half, generating USD540 million in revenue, already exceeding the USD500 million recorded for all of last year.

Ubtech Robotics, the Chinese firm behind the Walker series, ranked first worldwide last year, with revenue of CNY870 million (USD130 million), shipments of nearly 13,840 units, and an almost 25 percent revenue share, according to the report. The Shenzhen-based company retained the top spot in the first half, when revenue reached CNY620 million, and sales exceeded 16,120 units.

China's Agibot, Unitree Robotics, Galbot, and Leju Robotics Technology followed Ubtech in the ranking. Overseas companies, including Tesla and Figure AI, remain largely at the prototype iteration and internal-use stages, the report said.

Frost & Sullivan divides humanoid robot applications into four categories: entertainment performances, scientific research and education, data collection, and production operations.

Production operations recorded the strongest revenue growth among the four application areas. Global sales of humanoid robots used in production operations totaled 700 units last year, generating USD47 million in revenue. Sales in the segment climbed to 1,200 units in the first half of this year, while revenue reached USD78 million, up 66 percent from the total for all of 2025.

Meanwhile, the entertainment performance market -- the largest segment -- remained broadly stable, while the scientific research and education market declined slightly. Data collection applications were also largely unchanged in scale and were mainly used to support embodied artificial intelligence model training.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: Chinese Firms Eye Southeast Asia as Next Frontier for Growth, FutureChina Forum Speakers Say
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 29 -- Chinese companies are increasingly turning to Southeast Asia for new markets and supply-chain opportunities as the country shifts toward higher-value industries and seeks to boost domestic consumption, speakers said at the recent FutureChina Global Forum in Singapore.

Discussions at the 17th edition of the forum, which was organized by Business China, focused on China’s next phase of growth as it enters its 15th Five-Year Plan for 2026 to 2030, highlighting the country’s economic transition, the rise of artificial intelligence and the Association of Southeast Asian Nation’s role amid intensifying regional and global competition.

Emphasis was put on higher-value sectors including electric vehicles, batteries, artificial intelligence and advanced manufacturing. The need for stronger consumer demand to support broader economic growth was also addressed.

As high-tech manufacturing expands faster than domestic consumption, Chinese companies are looking overseas for new markets and building supply, production and consumer networks across Southeast Asia, according to discussions at the forum, which brought together more than 1,400 participants from over 1,000 organisations over a two-day period from Sept. 24 to Sept. 25.

At the same time, efforts to manage the property market and strengthen social and job security, as well as durable income growth, were highlighted as factors that could support consumer confidence in China.

ASEAN’s role in the regional economy was another focus of the forum. Speakers discussed the need to maintain the region’s openness as competition intensifies, while strengthening connections across financial systems, data infrastructure and energy networks.

Singapore will work with other ASEAN members as it takes on the bloc’s chairmanship in 2027, said Singapore Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry Gan Kim Yong, who opened the main forum as Guest of Honour.

“We want an ASEAN that remains open to the world with the capabilities, connections, and agencies to be able to shape our own future,” Gan said.

The forum also examined the implications of artificial intelligence for businesses and economies.

Singapore’s advantage would depend on turning AI into practical outcomes rather than competing with larger economies on computing power, chips or frontier models, Singapore Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information and Health Tan Kiat How said at a dedicated AI Track session.

Speakers at the AI sessions discussed China’s manufacturing and deployment capabilities as an advantage for embodied AI, while stressing the importance of real-world data, workforce retraining and organizational changes to ensure that AI delivers practical business value.

Participants also explored potential cooperation between Singapore and China, particularly by combining China’s engineering and manufacturing capabilities with Singapore’s business and governance environment.

Singapore needs to remain relevant in a more fragmented global economy by recognizing diverse perspectives within society, Singapore Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence Chan Chun Sing said at the main forum. For ASEAN, he highlighted the need for closer connections across finance, data and energy as areas that could support regional competitiveness.

The FutureChina Global Forum was launched in 2010 by Business China as a platform for dialogue on China’s development and its engagement with Singapore, ASEAN and the wider world.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: Chinese Carmaker GAC Hits Daily Limit Up After Unveiling Plan to Acquire Half of FAW Toyota
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 29 -- GAC Group’s stock price rose by its daily trading limit after the Chinese state-owned carmaker revealed a plan to acquire a 50 percent stake in FAW Toyota Motor, a joint venture between China Faw, a subsidiary of FAW Group, and Japan's Toyota Motor.

GAC [SHA: 601238], whose shares resumed trading on the Shanghai Stock Exchange today, closed 10 percent higher at CNY5.60 (84 US cents).

GAC will acquire FAW’s stake in FAW Toyota through a share issuance, the Guangzhou-based company said yesterday. GAC announced on Sept. 14 that it had signed a letter of intent to acquire a partial stake in a vehicle manufacturing JV of FAW without naming the target company.

The deal’s value has yet to be determined, GAC said. It has proposed an initial price of CNY5.75 per share, with the final number of shares issued to be determined by the agreed value of the transaction, the firm added.

GAC intends to raise additional funds by issuing shares to no more than 35 qualified investors. The proceeds, capped at 100 percent of the transaction value, will be used to fund the target project, replenish working capital, repay debt and cover related taxes, fees, and intermediary expenses.

Through the deal, FAW Toyota will become a GAC joint venture and China FAW will become GAC's second-largest shareholder. Toyota and its Chinese subsidiaries own the other half of the JV.

Separately, China FAW and GAC Industry, the parent groups of FAW and GAC respectively, signed a cooperation framework agreement today. The companies said they will deepen collaboration in areas including capital and asset linkages, technology innovation, and cross-regional coordination of industrial resources.

GAC’s preliminary plan said the transaction is expected to boost its investment income and net profit while creating greater synergies between FAW Toyota and GAC Toyota in research and development, supply chain management, manufacturing, and marketing, thereby reducing duplicated investment.

Founded in 2000, FAW Toyota is headquartered in Tianjin and has registered capital of USD3.29 billion. Its operations span Tianjin, Changchun, and Chengdu, covering passenger vehicle R&D, manufacturing, and sales, as well as production of engines and other key components, supply chain management, marketing and after-sales services.

As of June 30, FAW Toyota had unaudited total assets of CNY43.1 billion (USD6.4 billion), liabilities of CNY13.4 billion, and shareholders' equity of CNY29.7 billion, according to GAC. During the first half, the JV had a net profit of around CNY1 billion (USD150 million) on revenue of nearly CNY41 billion.

Combined sales volume at FAW Toyota and GAC Toyota accounted for 17 percent of all sales of passenger cars produced by Chinese joint ventures, GAC said, citing figures from the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: Can International Racing Accelerate the Globalization of Chinese Motorcycle Brands?
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 29 -- Chinese motorcycle manufacturers have burst onto the international scene in recent years as global racing becomes more than a test of speed and engineering and emerges as a powerful platform for building brands and winning fans around the world.

China’s exports of motorcycles surged 18 percent in the first seven months from a year earlier to 8.98 million bikes, and their export value soared 22.9 percent to USD6.2 billion. At this pace, full-year exports could exceed 15 million units, accounting for more than 60 percent of the country's total motorcycle production.

For a long time, Southeast Asia and Africa have been the main export markets for Chinese motorbikes. But this picture is changing. Chinese motorcycle manufacturers are moving toward models with larger engine capacities and higher-value-added products. Breakthroughs by brands like CFMOTO and Zhangxue Garage in international racing circuits are accelerating this shift.

On Sept. 14, at the 14th round of the 2026 MotoGP season, rider David Alonso from the CFMOTO Aspar Team clinched victory in the Moto3 race. A week later, 13-year-old Chinese rider Sun Shengbo from the CFMOTO Aspar Junior Team won a race at the Navarra round of the Spanish Superbike Championship. He also secured the overall annual championship in the ESBK Talent class ahead of schedule, becoming the first Chinese road-racing rider to be crowned annual champion in Spain's top-level youth racing series.

When asked why CFMOTO had chosen to invest in expensive top-tier international racing, Vice President Chen Zhiyong told Yicai, “Do you want to win a long-term war, or do you just want to win a single battle?”

“We want to be world-class and make our mark in motorsports. Our ultimate goal is to achieve 'Chinese bikes, Chinese riders, on Chinese tracks' at the highest level. This means doing things that are long-term, difficult, but right, rather than taking the easy route to gain short-lived publicity or attention.”

China Speed

CFMOTO made its debut at the EICMA motorcycle show in Milan in 2005, marking the beginning of its push into the European market. Since 2014, the Hangzhou-based company has maintained top market share in Europe’s All-Terrain Vehicle segment. In 2024, it deepened its localization layout by acquiring European brand GOES.

After nearly two decades of developing its presence in local markets, CFMOTO entered MotoGP, the world’s premier motorcycle racing championship, in 2022, becoming the first Chinese manufacturer to compete in the series. In 2024, CFMOTO teamed up with the legendary Spanish team Aspar, which boasts a 40-year history, penning a long-term agreement that runs through 2031.

Jorge Martínez, founder of Valencia-based Aspar, said he first saw CFMOTO’s vision for global expansion about 10 years ago. It aligned perfectly with his own vision for the "Aspar Universe," an ecosystem integrating riders, racing and the broader motorcycle industry.

"I found that Aspar and CFMOTO share the same philosophy. We both want to dedicate many years working together to accomplish a major project like this," Martínez said. He stressed that the partnership was not an easy decision. It was only after visiting CFMOTO’s factory a few years ago that he gained confidence in the brand.

"I have worked with Aprilia and Ducati, but CFMOTO’s pace of development was completely different. I witnessed 'China Speed' with my own eyes," he said.

Brand Amplifier

Racing is becoming an amplifier of brand value. At the showroom of Jets Marivent, CFMOTO’s exclusive distributor in Spain, team logos and images of star riders occupy prominent positions.

The distributor’s head told Yicai that CFMOTO commands a 46 percent share of Spain's four-wheel ATV market, making it the market leader. Meanwhile, its 450MT off-road motorbike series has become highly popular and the firm had already achieved its full-year sales target by September.

The executive said CFMOTO has used Spain’s deep-rooted racing culture and localized marketing strategies to build closer connections with local consumers and strengthen brand recognition. The expansion of its retail network has been a direct result of that growing awareness. CFMOTO now has more than 40 stores in the region and plans to accelerate the rollout of new outlets.

Compared with established European and Japanese motorcycle brands, Chinese manufacturers have proved particularly adept at social media and content marketing. They have been able to bring together fans, brands and teams, creating an emotional connection that transcends the technology itself.

Teams maintain accounts on both Chinese and international social media platforms and use activities such as race-day content and live broadcasts featuring riders to engage directly with fans. At races, CFMOTO Aspar Team staff are often approached by fans who recognize them and actively greet them, a sign that racing is helping turn spectators into brand enthusiasts.

This fan loyalty is also translating into merchandise revenue. CFMOTO said sales of branded merchandise have continued to rise. At the recent MotoGP event at the Misano World Circuit in Italy, CFMOTO T-shirts sold out quickly.

Chinese brands have their own strengths in community building, social media and content distribution, said Carlos Ezpeleta, chief sporting officer of Dorna Sports, the sports and entertainment group that operates MotoGP.

Chinese manufacturers have an opportunity to combine products, brands, communities and events to create greater value rather than simply focusing on technological research and development, he said.

Long-Term Mindset

"What Chinese firms currently lack most is a long-term mindset," Chen said. “Short-term efforts to attract attention cannot sustain a brand over the long run. Only by competing alongside the best can we drive technological development."

He summarized this approach with the Chinese slogan "self-strength makes everything strong," which means that only by building its own capabilities can a company truly establish a firm foothold in global competition.

For CFMOTO, racing is not an expensive showcase but an accelerator for technological development. Chen said the firm’s "racing-driven research and development" strategy is more than a slogan.

CFMOTO’s flagship V4 SR-RR superbike, launched this year, is powered by a self-developed V4 engine and set a Chinese motorcycle speed record of 315.82 kilometers per hour. Key technologies used in this model, including engine performance tuning, aerodynamic design and electronic-control calibration, have directly benefited from data accumulated and validated on the track through CFMOTO’s MotoGP program.

Ezpeleta noted that much of the technology now widely applied in high-performance production bikes today was developed through decades of competition in racing. Manufacturers have to keep innovating and improving technological efficiency, he said.

So can international racing accelerate the globalization of Chinese motorcycle brands? The answer is yes. But the acceleration is not necessarily in shipment volumes. Rather, it is about reshaping the position of Chinese companies in the global industry from "suppliers" to "partners," and ultimately to “rule-shapers.”

There is one prerequisite for this acceleration and that is staying on the track long enough. As Chen put it, firms need to do things that are “long-term, difficult, but right.”

The real race has only just begun.

Editor: Kim Taylor
